p2.summary: Retained Axe attachments contain unresolved incomplete diagnostics in addition to zero violations.
p2.evidence: The full result packet contains 1,320 accessibility attachments: zero violation rule entries/nodes; 209 color-contrast incomplete rule entries covering 1,006 nodes; and 24 aria-valid-attr-value incomplete entries covering 24 nodes. The color-contrast diagnostics are Axe inability to determine background/text for image-containing, partially obscured, overlapped, non-text or short-text nodes. The aria diagnostics are 12 menu and 12 popover aria-controls references that Axe cannot resolve through the custom-element boundary.
p2.actualVsExpected: The maintained suites assert an empty Axe violations list and reject prohibited-ARIA incomplete checks. They retain other incomplete checks for review; no required test failed.
p2.consequence: These diagnostics do not establish complete WCAG or assistive-technology compliance for the affected cases.
p2.priorityRationale: Nonblocking follow-up: no Axe violation or prohibited-ARIA incomplete was observed; the packet and this review disclose the unresolved checks; manual assistive-technology certification is explicitly deferred rather than claimed.
p2.recommendedCorrection: Add targeted contrast assertions for the affected rendered states and a custom-element-boundary aria-controls check, then supplement with the deferred manual assistive-technology review before making a stronger compliance claim.
p2.verification: Repeat the full matrix and confirm the incomplete diagnostic counts are reduced or explicitly justified without introducing violations.

limitations: The independent reviewer parsed the retained 1,137-case result rather than rerunning the complete matrix; the focused Firefox six-case repeat was independently rerun 18/18 across three repetitions.
No manual VoiceOver, NVDA or other assistive-technology certification was performed or claimed.
The retained visual matrix and reviewed captures prove the owned fixtures and states, not universal pixel equivalence for every consumer environment or operating system.
The adverse visualization timing is a desktop Chromium observation with no universal timing threshold; it is not field or lower-powered-device evidence.
The Node 22 site-browser false start is environmental and excluded from qualification; only the pinned Node 24 rerun is counted.
This review does not qualify T30, T31, T40, publication, deployment, release promotion or live-site identity.

verdict.summary: The exact current-source T29 author packet is internally consistent and independently checked in the retained evidence plus the prescribed focused Firefox repeat. No P0 or P1 finding remains. One explicitly disclosed P2 records unresolved Axe incomplete diagnostics, and a long-number horizontal-scroll observation remains nonblocking; the evidence supports T29 approval with those limits and without a stronger manual-AT or universal-compliance claim.
